idiom_name: class over mutable.Map with an ArrayBuffer[Operation] journal
implementation_notes: A Scala trait is the collaborator abstraction and the recording fake is a class - or an anonymous new Ledger { ... } - holding a mutable.Map for state and a mutable.ArrayBuffer[Operation] for the journal, so the classic structure collapses into an ordinary declaration and no framework is needed for working behaviour. ScalaMock's stubs and mocks record calls and verify them (verify(...), .calls, .times) without implementing behaviour, so they cover the stub and mock rows; its newer stub API even exposes the recorded calls list, which is the library-side equivalent of this journal. Keep the fake per test - an object (singleton) is shared across the suite - prefer immutable case classes for journal entries so assertions compare by value, and snapshot the buffer with toList before exposing it.
pitfalls: mutable.Map and ArrayBuffer are not thread-safe, and a fake defined in an object is shared across the whole suite - create it per test.
A loosely typed mock factory or implicit injection can install a fake of the wrong trait instance; type the fake against the exact trait the code under test consumes.
Anonymous instantiations capture the enclosing test scope and cannot be reused or inspected; promote to a named class once the journal matters.
